description:
The TLS client wrappers take an *optional* identity binding:

    pub fn verify_tls_client_dns<P, R>(
        chain: &[Certificate],
        anchors: &[TrustAnchor],
        identity: Option<&ServerName<'_>>,   // <-- optional
        profile: &P,
        now_unix: u64,
        revocation: &R,
    ) -> crate::Result<ValidatedPath>;

    pub fn verify_tls_client_mailbox<P, R>(
        ...
        identity: Option<&MailboxName<'_>>,   // <-- optional
        ...
    );

The rustdoc rationale (src/lib.rs:776-787 and similar) — \"callers fall
into two camps... pin a DNS or IP identity in the SAN, or callers that
want path-only validation\" — applies equally to S/MIME. An MTA
operator validating inbound S/MIME signatures may want chain validity
+ EKU enforcement (`emailProtection`) but read the identity out of the
RFC 5322 From header, not the cert SAN. A document-archiving system
may want to verify the chain validates and the cert was for S/MIME use
at all, deferring identity binding to a different layer.

But:

    pub fn verify_smime_signer<P, R>(
        chain: &[Certificate],
        anchors: &[TrustAnchor],
        mailbox: &MailboxName<'_>,   // <-- required
        ...
    );

    pub fn verify_smime_recipient<P, R>(
        ...
        mailbox: &MailboxName<'_>,   // <-- required
        ...
    );

There's no way to invoke these wrappers without supplying a mailbox.
Callers wanting the EKU + KU enforcement that the recipient/signer
profile encodes, without identity binding, are forced to:

1. Drop down to `verify_chain` directly, AND
2. Reimplement the profile EKU/KU enforcement themselves (since the
   wrapper does it via the supplied Profile, and the wrapper body is
   the thing pulling that profile into play).

This is the api-contract,defensive smell: a wrapper exists for the
common case, but the slightly-less-common case (path-only S/MIME
validation) is *worse* served than if no wrapper existed at all
(because the caller has to recreate the wrapper logic).

Suggested fix: change both signatures to `mailbox: Option<&MailboxName<'_>>`,
matching `verify_tls_client_mailbox`. Body is one `if let Some(m) = mailbox`
guard, identical to the TLS-client side. The signer-vs-recipient distinction
remains in the caller-supplied Profile (which is the contract anyway,
per PKIX-q9hv.5).

Caller impact: MTAs / document-archiving / batch S/MIME validators
that read identity from a non-cert source.
title: verify_smime_signer/recipient take required mailbox; no path-only mode
